@@ -1617,6 +1617,20 @@
 > Note: When using Unity, dynamic code generation only works when targeting .NET Framework 4.x + mono runtime.
 For all other Unity targets, AOT is required.
 
+### Opting out of source generation
+
+A `[MessagePackObject]` type can opt out of source generation with `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`.
+No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which use reflection, so such a type is not AOT-safe.
+
+The analyzer still validates these types, because they are serialized at run time and must still have a valid contract:
+- Members have a `[Key]` or `[IgnoreMember]` attribute ([MsgPack004](doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md)).
+- Keys are unique and all of the same kind ([MsgPack005](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md)).
+- Non-public members require `AllowPrivate` ([MsgPack015](doc/analyzers/MsgPack015.md)).
+- Members have types that are themselves serializable ([MsgPack003](doc/analyzers/MsgPack003.md)).
+- Types are accessible to the resolver ([MsgPack012](doc/analyzers/MsgPack012.md)).
+
+The analyzer does not report the partial-class requirement ([MsgPack011](doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md)) or the AOT-only checks ([MsgPack016](doc/analyzers/MsgPack016.md) and [MsgPack017](doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md)) for these types, because they only apply when a formatter is generated.
+
 ### Customizations
 
 You can customize the generated source through properties on the `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute`.

runs.reply:
Nothing was built or run (no .NET SDK here), so both the fix and the new tests are reasoned from the code only.

The crash was in the explicit-`[Key]` path of the type collector: a repeated key, or a key of the other kind (int vs. string), was reported and then still used, which threw. `SuppressSourceGeneration` turned out not to matter; the same crash happens with or without it.

Files changed:

- [TypeCollector.cs:722](src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:722) — the fix:
  - **Analyzer:** a member with a repeated, mixed or null key now gets its `MsgPack005` error and is left out of the member tables, in both the property and the field loop.
  - **Generator:** a type with any such key gets no formatter at all, rather than one missing the offending member.
  - **Constructor matching:** skipped for such a type, since it would only produce misleading `MsgPack007` errors against an incomplete member list.
  - **Null key on a field:** `[Key(null)]` on a field crashed the same way and is fixed too; its message now names the type and member.
- [MsgPack00xAnalyzerTests.cs:95](tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/MsgPack00xAnalyzerTests.cs:95) — new `NullStringKey_Field`, `DuplicateKeys` and `MixedKeys` tests; the last two run with and without `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`.
- [GenerationTests.cs:711](tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/GenerationTests.cs:711) — new `InvalidKeys_NoFormatterGenerated` test: a duplicate or mixed key yields `MsgPack005` and no generated source.

Two things I left alone:

- **Map mode:** it still drops the second of two same-named members from the generated formatter (the analyzer reports `MsgPack018`). That is existing behaviour outside this bug, but it is the same "quietly drop a member" pattern, so say if you want it changed too.
- **`[Key(null)]` on a record's primary-constructor property:** this still hits an unguarded cast in the null-key diagnostic. It is a separate cause from the repeated/mixed-key crash.

runs.reply:
The analyzer no longer crashes on a repeated or mixed key; it reports MsgPack005 on the offending member and carries on. Nothing was built or run (no .NET SDK here), so the code and the new tests are checked by reading only.

The generator, which shares this code, now emits no formatter at all for a type with an unusable key, rather than one that silently skips the member. That also applies to two cases that did not crash before (`[Key(null)]` on a property, and an int key on a property after a string key), which used to get a formatter minus that member.

Files changed:

- [TypeCollector.cs](src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs) — the fix.
  - Properties and fields now share one key-handling helper (`AddKeyedMember`), replacing two diverging copies; it reports duplicate, mixed and null keys instead of throwing.
  - A type with such a key returns no model, checked last so every other diagnostic is still reported.
  - `[Key(null)]` on a record primary-constructor property no longer hits a bad cast.
  - The null-key message on fields now carries the type and member name.
  - Attribute arguments are read through a length-checked helper, so a half-typed `[Key]`, `[MessagePackFormatter]`, `[MessagePackObject(...)]` or `[Union]` cannot throw.
- [AnalyzerUtilities.cs](src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Utils/AnalyzerUtilities.cs) — same length guard for the assembly-level `MessagePackKnownFormatter` and `MessagePackAssumedFormattable` attributes.
- [MessagePackCodeFixProvider.cs](src/MessagePack.Analyzers.CodeFixes/CodeFixes/MessagePackCodeFixProvider.cs) — same guard where the code fix reads existing `[Key]` values.
- [MsgPack00xAnalyzerTests.cs](tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/MsgPack00xAnalyzerTests.cs) — new tests for duplicate int keys, duplicate string keys, mixed keys and a null key on a field, each with and without `SuppressSourceGeneration = true`, plus a null key on a record primary constructor.
- [GenerationTests.cs](tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/GenerationTests.cs) — one generator test asserting that duplicate and mixed keys produce the diagnostics and no generated formatter.
- [MsgPack005.md](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md) — documents the three key conditions and that no formatter is generated for such a type.

Two things I left as they were:

- **Map-mode name collisions (MsgPack018):** the generator still emits a formatter without the hidden base member. Changing that would alter existing generator output for anyone who suppressed that error.
- **Constructor checks:** they still run against the members that remain, so a type with a bad key can also get MsgPack007. The record test expects exactly that.

@@ -4,3 +4,35 @@ Invalid MessagePackObject definition.
 
 There are a variety of conditions that can produce this diagnostic.
 Examine the specific message to understand what is wrong and how to correct it.
+
+## Conditions that concern `[Key]` attributes
+
+Message | Cause | Correction
+--|--|--
+Both int and string keys are null | A member is attributed with `[Key(null)]`. | Give the member an integer or a (non-null) string key.
+All KeyAttribute arguments must be of the same type (either string or int) | A type uses integer keys on some members and string keys on others. The first attributed member (properties are considered before fields) decides which kind the type uses. | Use one kind of key for all the members of the type.
+All KeyAttribute arguments must be unique | Two members of a type, or of a type and its base types, have the same key. | Give each member its own key.
+
+These are reported whether or not a formatter is source generated for the type,
+since they are just as invalid for a type declared with `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`,
+for which the dynamic resolver would otherwise throw at runtime.
+
+For example:
+
+```cs
+[MessagePackObject]
+public class A
+{
+    [Key(0)]
+    public int First { get; set; }
+
+    [Key(0)] // MsgPack005: this key is already taken by First
+    public int Second { get; set; }
+
+    [Key("third")] // MsgPack005: the other keys of this type are integers
+    public int Third { get; set; }
+}
+```
+
+No formatter is source generated for a type that has any of these problems:
+a formatter that silently skipped the offending members would be worse than none.
